newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Opp'n seeks evidence from RBA chief.
newsitem.headline: Australian Opp'n seeks evidence from RBA chief.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition said on Thursday it would ask Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane to appear before a parliamentary committee to explain the bank's recent sale of most of its gold reserves.
Opposition assistant treasury spokesman Nick Sherry said in a statement he would ask Macfarlane to testify at an August 18 hearing of the Senate economic legislative committee.

Macfarlane would be asked to explain the bank's decision-making process, the budgetary implications of the sale, the role of Treasurer Peter Costello and the bank's measures for dealing with issues of conflict of interest.
The central bank announced on July 4 that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold -- two thirds of its total reserves -- over the previous six months.
The government has defended the sale as prudent and in the national interest.
Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday he would inquire into the role of bank director and mining chief Hugh Morgan in the bank's decision.
But Morgan, head of WMC Ltd, said late on Thursday he had never used information gained in his capacity as a board member to benefit WMC, or passed any such information to company officials.
